title: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

sense.text:
“Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad.” When you see oppression, you are going to be mad for what you see. If you are wise, you will be angry when you see oppression. The reason so many brothers have no racial anger is that they do not see themselves as oppressed, and they do not see their people as oppressed. They say things like, I wasn’t a slave, that was a long time ago; Jesus is love, my brother, forgive your enemy. They got a good job and they are making money, and it is not until the oppression hits them that they come asking where the black people are.

“And a gift destroyeth the heart.” The gift is the job. For some brothers the gift is the white woman, and that thing destroys them. The gift is civil rights, civil privileges, inclusion: it destroyed us as a people, because now you think you are equal to them when you are at the bottom and they are at the top.

This is why the Edomite showrunner fired the actor who played the angry god Mr. Nancy in American Gods: his character was promoting anger, pushing that Ecclesiastes 7:7 spirit into our people, and they did not want angry black people. The black friends on the set who agreed with getting rid of him were Pharaoh’s taskmasters’ officers. That is the seasoning process: it rewarded good behavior, compliance, and punished bad behavior, and racial anger was the bad behavior.

The slave makers knew that our forefathers fresh from the continent had to be broken in, forced to accept a subservient position. Is that in the Bible? Of course it is. He “shall wear out the saints of the most High.” To wear out is to break in: to make us seasoned and subservient, to destroy us.

precepts.why:
“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

That is the breaking in: cut off from our heritage and made to serve our enemies in a land we did not know. The slave makers wrote that strong men in succeeding generations would only wear the yoke of bondage if their psychology was altered, if they were made to believe they were innately inferior and to accept slavery as their natural condition.

That innate inferiority is still in the back of the mind of our people: you’re nothing, you’re a gentile, the white man is God. It shows when you argue that Jeremiah 14:2 does not mean what it says, when you say they cannot be saved, when you celebrate New Year’s, Christmas and Thanksgiving, when you worship a God that does not look like you, when you say his color doesn’t matter. Everybody worships a God that looks like them. It shows when you glorify the ghetto and the trap: that is accepting the bottom as your natural condition.

sense.text:
The seasoned slaves taught the new arrivals their new names. “And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

A proverb is a saying: you’re a slave, a savage, murderous, prone to violence. A byword is a name called outside your God-given name, whether it is self-given or given to you by force: a byword is a false name. And it is “among all nations” that we fall under this, wherever the Lord led us by ship.

On the plantation the overseer and master were the ultimate authority: if a slave denied it, food was withheld. “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee”: serve as a slave, under enemies the Lord sent against us.

“In hunger”: when you want food, he can deprive you of it. “And in thirst”: he can deprive you of water. “And in nakedness”: of clothing. “And in want of all things”: whatever you want, education, a home, a place to stay, living in general, the enemy is the one who provides it.

“And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee”: until you are broken in, until you are no longer you anymore. The iron slave collar clamped around the runaway’s neck is that yoke.

That is why it says wear out until you are destroyed: God meant that thing. The trauma our people faced in slavery has been shown to alter our DNA; Esau literally damaged us. Our forefathers were destroyed psychologically while trying to raise their babies, and the babies grew up unstable. The master became the father, the imprint for male behavior, and we adopted the thoughts and behaviors of Edom. Today we are those children, and that is why we read this Bible daily: because of the damage that was done and passed on to us.

In the 1940s our forefathers would beat their male children severely at any sign of that spark of anger, so they would fall in line with the white man and not go through what they went through. That is the breaking process.

“For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.” Where are these things found? In the heart of men. The heart in the Bible is the mind, the brain.

precepts.why:
“A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance”: what is in the heart shows in your face. “But by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.” By the sorrow of the mind the spirit is broken.

Did we have sorrow of mind in slavery? Every day. Did we face trauma? Every day. That is how the spirit of our people was broken: through the mind.

“Hope deferred maketh the heart sick”: hope deferred makes the mind sick. During slavery our hope was deferred in every way: watching our people hung, castrated, beaten, raped, stripped from their families, shipped off, fed to dogs, heads cut off, thrown in a hot box, yoked to the bottom of a ship. That is hope deferred.

“But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.” This truth is that desire. When it is acquired, it is a tree of life, and that is what helps to heal the damage Esau did to us.

sense.text:
Christ is speaking through Isaiah: “The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek.” Good tidings is good news, the gospel. The meek are those who submit themselves to the Lord.

“He hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted.” Brokenhearted does not mean a romance, some emotional R&B song. It means broken-minded: your mind is destroyed, your mind is broken. The crowd of forty to sixty thousand in that pastor’s coliseum was a crowd of brokenhearted people: broken people.

“To proclaim liberty to the captives”: if we are broken-minded, we are captive. When Christ was born on this earth in the time of Rome, we were captives. “And the opening of the prison to them that are bound”: we are in prison, serving a sentence. We are in America because we broke God’s laws. We are not here to get compensated with reparations; we are here to live out a prison sentence. You may get off on good behavior, meaning you get delivered, but some are going to stay in jail till they die. We are a nation of inmates.

And those not in America, in Jamaica, Antigua, Papua New Guinea, Trinidad and Tobago, Puerto Rico, Madagascar, Nigeria, Brazil, Curaçao, South Africa, were born in colonies. America itself is an extension of Britain. These are slave colonies, and we are slaves in them.

“To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God.” The acceptable year of the Lord is the day of vengeance: revenge, God’s revenge. That is acceptable in the eyes of God.

“To comfort all that mourn”: we have no comfort.

“To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion”: not all nations, Zion. We are Zion. “To give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness.” We are in the spirit of heaviness because we are not home. “That they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, that he might be glorified”: brought home, and he gets the glory.

Some of our people would rather have the white heaven of Uncle Ruckus: bleaching the skin, dyeing the hair blonde, praising a white God. Christianity is the perfection of slavery. If slavery did not fully destroy you, Christianity comes to bring you under subjection to serve and worship the white man, and you hate yourself.

“For, lo, thine enemies make a tumult: and they that hate thee have lifted up the head. They have taken crafty counsel against thy people”: they gained power and conspired against God’s people, “and consulted against thy hidden ones.”

“Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” How? By the seasoning process, by the trauma process: destroying us, breaking us in, wearing us out.

“They have consulted together with one consent: they are confederate against thee”: against God and his people. “The tabernacles of Edom” is the first, the ringleader of the whole thing: the so-called white man. “The Ishmaelites” are the Arabs. Moab is the Chinese, “the Hagarenes” are Muslims, Gebal is Hamites, Ammon is the Japanese, Amalek is the Israelis, the Philistines more Hamites, and “the inhabitants of Tyre” are the Canaanites that inhabited West Africa. These are the ones that were instrumental in enslaving us.

“Which perished at En–dor: they became as dung for the earth”: these nations were destroyed before. “Make their nobles like Oreb, and like Zeeb: yea, all their princes as Zebah, and as Zalmunna”: the ones we destroyed.

“Who said, Let us take to ourselves the houses of God in possession.” The houses of God are the house of Judah, the house of Benjamin, the house of Ephraim, the house of Asher. That is what these nations said, and that is what they did.

precepts.why:
“I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men.” The Most High said it before the nations ever said, Let the name of Israel be no more in remembrance.

How was our remembrance made to cease? By breaking us in, wearing us out, destroying us: the seasoning and the trauma.

sense.text:
“I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” Our nation is likened to a comely and delicate woman.

Dr. Joy DeGruy saw it in South Africa: the children of Ndebele, living in their villages with somewhat freedom, were quiet, confident, humble and secure, knowing their roles without being told. But the people of Onverwacht, descendants of our people enslaved by the Dutch and living among Esau, carried slave names, had lost their tribe and tongue, held their heads low, would not look anyone in the eye, and had drugs, alcohol, domestic violence, crime and poverty, with children unruly and violent. It is the same thing back home in America. That is what living among Edom does to our people.

precepts.why:
“But if a man find a betrothed damsel in the field, and the man force her, and lie with her: then the man only that lay with her shall die: but unto the damsel thou shalt do nothing; there is in the damsel no sin worthy of death.” “For he found her in the field, and the betrothed damsel cried”: she fought against him; she did not want to lie with him, but he forced her, “and there was none to save her.”

Why read this? Because that is what Edom did to the nation of Israel. They took us by force and broke us, the same way this man forced this woman. “For as when a man riseth against his neighbour, and slayeth him, even so is this matter”: did he kill her? No, but he killed her spirit. He broke her mind. That is what happened to us, and there was none to save us either. It is parallel.

That is trauma. What is Esau writing over us in this context? Death, in every syllable of the word: as a nation, not as individuals, as a whole.

“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.” No man shall buy you: none to save you. It is the same thing as the damsel in the field. There was none to save her, and there was none to save us.

sense.text:
“Now also many nations are gathered against thee”: all of them gathered against Israel, “that say, Let her be defiled.” When a woman gets raped, is she not defiled? Yes. Let her, Israel the woman, be defiled: let her spirit stay broken. “And let our eye look upon Zion”: watch her and make sure she stays that way.

The Godfather showed it: the council of mob bosses agreed to keep the drug traffic among the dark people, the coloreds, because they’re animals anyway, so let them lose their souls. Let them be defiled. Italian, Russian, Irish, Dutch: whatever their nationality, they all understood to keep the drugs among black and brown people and keep us destroyed. Crack babies. In Godfather of Harlem the mob boss tells Bumpy Johnson he sells drugs in Harlem not for the money but because every junkie, every hungry child and every baby born with a habit makes his heart sing. To see a man defiled and destroyed: that is the nations, all of them.

The triad told the drug dealer the same thing: black people are the trendsetters, but they have no unity, very easy to break up. A nation divided shall not stand, and that is why Esau divides us in the colonies we were born in. A nurse in Virginia was arrested for breaking the bones of black newborn babies in a NICU, and released on bond. Let her be defiled.

precepts.why:
“All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem”: the woman, Israel. “Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?” This is God’s people? These Negroes in the ghettos and slums, twerking on the video? The nations look at us and mock.

“All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee”: all the many nations speak ill of us. “They say, We have swallowed her up: certainly this is the day that we looked for; we have found, we have seen it.” Where did they find it? In our Bibles. They read it: if Israel sinned against their God, they could conquer them, and keep these people destroyed.

“The Lord hath done that which he had devised; he hath fulfilled his word that he had commanded in the days of old: he hath thrown down, and hath not pitied”: no mercy. “And he hath caused thine enemy to rejoice over thee”: sent us as gifts, as slaves to our enemies. “He hath set up the horn of thine adversaries”: lifted up the head of our enemies and gave them power over us and over the planet, because of our disobedience.

sense.text: “But this is a people robbed and spoiled”: robbed and corrupted. “They are all of them snared in holes, and they are hid in prison houses”: captivity, religions, philosophies, doctrines. “They are for a prey”: preyed upon. “And none delivereth”: none will save; no one tried to save us at all. “For a spoil, and none saith, Restore”: none says bring them back, gather them together again, reunite them.
“Who among you will give ear to this? who will hearken and hear for the time to come?”

precepts.why: Where none saith Restore, the Lord says, “For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord.” Why? “Because they called thee an Outcast, saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after.” Nobody cares about those black people over there; let them stay where they are.

“All that found them have devoured them”: the same as the enemies in Lamentations who said they had swallowed her up. “And their adversaries said, We offend not”: I didn’t do it, my fathers did that, it has nothing to do with me, it’s none of my business.

“Because they have sinned against the Lord, the habitation of justice, even the Lord, the hope of their fathers.” They broke their God’s laws, so how is that our fault? Us not saving them is their problem, not ours. That is what the nations say.

sense.text:
Some say they are not all like that; there are good ones. Muhammad Ali answered it: if ten thousand rattlesnakes are coming to bite you and a thousand of them mean no harm, they all look alike, so you shut the door. And when a white woman asked Malcolm X what she could do to help, he said nothing. That is common sense. A few good ones does not make them all good, and that is how God sees it.

“Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity builded the temple unto the Lord God of Israel; then they came to Zerubbabel, and to the chief of the fathers, and said unto them, Let us build with you: for we seek your God”. We’re good over here; we love your God too; we know Christ is black; we will keep the commandments with you. “And we do sacrifice unto him since the days of Esar–haddon king of Assur, which brought us up hither.”

“Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God.” They did not say, let the good ones come help. They did not say, let the ones with black babies come help. Nothing to do with us. “But we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel”: we ourselves, united together, “as king Cyrus the king of Persia hath commanded us.” The king gave us the allowance; we don’t need your help.

Then see what the good ones did: “Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building.” That was the purpose from the beginning: if you can’t beat them, join them, and destroy them from the inside. Our forefathers were smart and said, You can’t be around us; we see you.

precepts.why:
The same thing is repeated: “It is not for us and you to build together an house unto the Lord our God. We ourselves alone will build unto the Lord of Israel.” Not for us and you to build together, ever.

“But the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building; and by their secret plots”: to join us and stop us from the inside. Malcolm X said he respected the wolf more than the fox, because the wolf shows its fangs. The fox is the same as the wolf but more crafty: he smiles in your face while he is trying to kill your sheep. Christ called Herod a fox: crafty, deceitful, conniving, backstabbing. Many Israelites fall for the foxes.

“And popular persuasions and commotions”: today a popular persuasion is Christianity, I believe what you believe, liberal, conservative, the media and content creators. By these “they hindered the finishing of the building all the time that king Cyrus lived: so they were hindered from building for the space of two years, until the reign of Darius.”

sense.text:
What is Esau out to stop? “When Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, heard of it, it grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.” Sanballat the Horonite was a Moabite, Tobiah an Ammonite.

That is what these nations do not want: the rising of a black Messiah. Their aim is to disrupt, neutralize and destroy any rising of a black Messiah or black Messiahs. Martin King was deemed one, Malcolm was one, Stokely Carmichael, Kwame Ture, was one, Fred Hampton was one. Black unity is deemed a danger to national security; that is why they dissolved us in France. That has not changed.

precepts.why:
“For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people.” Mordecai sought the welfare of his people, as Nehemiah did. The Most High always raises up that spark in our brothers to rise up and seek the welfare of their people.

That is why Esau sits around finding ways to give us drugs, crack and cocaine, and to destroy our families and our minds through trauma: so that kind of man will not rise again. The Esthers, the Judiths, the Susannas, the Rebekahs, Shiphrah and Puah: they cannot be allowed to live. But they have all come back. If we are back, they are back, and the nations know it.
“They said one to another, Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” That is seeking out the welfare of our people.

“For it is better for us to die in battle, than to behold the calamities of our people and our sanctuary.” Esau could not have these kind of men: Mordecai, Nehemiah, Mattathias, Judas Maccabeus, Simon, Jonathan, Eleazar. Give them drugs, give them cocaine, break them in slavery, destroy them. But God said, No, that is not going to happen: I am going to raise them up before your eyes and destroy you.

sense.text: There are some among us just like Uncle Ruckus, praising white Jesus. “Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement.” Death and hell are the nations. “When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us”: when destruction comes, we’ll be safe. “For we have made lies our refuge”: Christianity, politics. “And under falsehood have we hid ourselves.”

precepts.why:
“In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us”: that is the covenant with hell and death. “For since we departed from them we have had much sorrow”: we have been miserable without the white man; the white man has got to be around.

“So this device pleased them well.” “Then certain of the people were so forward herein, that they went to the king, who gave them licence to do after the ordinances of the heathen”: they went and got legal permission to do evil.

sense.text: This is not all to be put on the white man. That gives you a way out, a cop-out. See how we were before the white man was around: “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.”
“By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood”: black on black on black crime.

“Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein shall languish.” There was evil all in Judea, before the white man’s influence. The evil the white man put upon us was already in us to begin with; he just enhanced it.

precepts.why:
“As for the beauty of his ornament, he set it in majesty”: he had us in our kingdom. “But they made the images of their abominations and of their detestable things therein”: we went to idolatry. “Therefore have I set it far from them. And I will give it into the hands of the strangers for a prey, and to the wicked of the earth for a spoil”: the land given to the wicked of the earth, the so-called white man, “and they shall pollute it.”

“For the robbers shall enter into it, and defile it”: the heathen entered our land and our temple, Edom included, and defiled it. “Make a chain” means establish slavery. “For the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.” Crime translates to sin: when you break God’s commandments, you are a criminal. Crime and violence were found among us before the white man was ever around. Nobody is going to say, the white man made me evil.

“Even of late my people is risen up as an enemy: ye pull off the robe with the garment from them that pass by securely.” We were robbing people, ripping people’s clothes off, robbing each other at sword point, the way they take your sneakers and your jacket today at gunpoint and knife point.

Edom did have an impact on our psyche. Alexander the Macedonian “reigned in his stead, the first over Greece, and made many wars, and won many strong holds, and slew the kings of the earth.” “So Alexander reigned twelve years, and then died. And his servants bare rule every one in his place. And after his death they all put crowns upon themselves”: Edom gained power on the earth. “So did their sons after them many years: and evils were multiplied in the earth.”

When Edom came into power, all the evil that was around multiplied. We were already wicked as hell, but around Edom the evil in us increased: it is enhanced, supported, nurtured, embraced by social media, the rap music, the environment we are in. That is why we are worse now than ever before. Like the Joker with Harvey Dent, all it needed was a little push, and he turned the good guy into himself. Edom did the exact same thing: turned us into him. But the spirit of Esau, of Cain, was already in us; the Pharisees had it, the elders that killed the prophets had it. While Edom was in the caves minding his own business, we were out here killing, fornicating, stealing, lying.

What keeps us connected to God, and the reason God fights for us, is keeping his laws. Esau understands that our weakness is breaking God’s laws, so he creates situations and pushes and enhances sin among our people, so that we stay in our sin and our God does not fight for us. That was Balaam’s counsel: the only way to get them is for them to sin, so send in the women. That is why the rap music that glorifies selling drugs, calling our women hoes, sex and murder is banned in other countries but pushed in America: to keep our people in sin. The sin is in us, but Esau exploits it and enhances it.

sense.text: “If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed; and ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.”

“They answered him, We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?” That is the brother today: I’m never a slave, I’m free, I got a six-figure job, a fancy car, a big house; I’m a high-value man; I don’t play victim.

“Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin.” When you break God’s laws and live in the midst of sin, you end up in bondage. Sin and bondage go hand in hand. The audience was full of Pharisees who were arrogant and said, We ain’t in bondage, but that was a front and a lie.

precepts.why:
Behind closed doors they said something else. “Then gathered the chief priests and the Pharisees a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many miracles. If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.”

I thought they were never in bondage to any man. Before the people: I’m in bondage to no man. Among themselves: if this man keeps teaching, the white man is going to take away our power, our position of authority in our nation. They knew they were in bondage.

“Behold your King!” “But they cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him.” Just as black folks cry, Free so-and-so, for straight-up killers, we chose a criminal, Barabbas, over our king to go free.

“Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar.” The white man is our king. They were in bondage to no man, yet they had a king over them giving them orders.

That is the well-off Negro today who says he is not oppressed and defends the white man as though he were his own father: commentators, podcasters and content creators who cry over Charlie Kirk but not over Trey Reed hung from a tree, who attack their own people for views, who are married into Edom, who call democracy our salvation. They quote the Bible all the time, but they will not quote John 19:15. That is them: no king but Caesar.

sense.text: “But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, whom he conquered.” Jason in the Bible hated his own countrymen, and Jason Whitlock, with the same name, is the same: he accused our bishop of being a racial idolater while he is a financial idolater, loving master with all his heart and soul, like all the rest of those men.

precepts.why:
“Then they that were with Maccabeus made supplication, and besought God that he would be their helper; and so they ran with violence upon the strong holds of the Idumeans”, “and slew all that fell into their hands, and killed no fewer than twenty thousand.” Nine thousand of the Idumeans fled into “two very strong castles, having all manner of things convenient to sustain the siege”, with food and supplies to keep them alive.

Maccabeus left Simon, Joseph and Zaccheus to besiege them. “Now they that were with Simon, being led with covetousness, were persuaded for money through certain of those that were in the castle, and took seventy thousand drachms, and let some of them escape.” Some of our people were paid off to let Esau escape.

Maccabeus “accused those men, that they had sold their brethren for money, and set their enemies free to fight against them.” Sold their brethren for money: financial idolaters. “So he slew those that were found traitors, and immediately took the two castles.” We killed traitors back then. Judas Iscariot killed himself.

“But Rhodocus, who was in the Jews’ host, disclosed the secrets to the enemies; therefore he was sought out, and when they had gotten him, they put him in prison.” Rhodocus was one of our people who sold us out and gave information to the enemy. Some in the camp right now are Rhodocus, women and brothers, FBI, CIA: that is on you.

sense.text: “And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.” The Herodians were supporters of Herod, black men supporting Rome. All the well-off Negroes, commentators and content creators named in the class are Herodians: supporters of America, supporters of Rome, supporters of money.

precepts.why:
“And they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to catch him in his words.” That is what these men do: have us on their shows and podcasts to catch us in our words, make fools of us and embarrass us to make content. Herodians.

We are ministers of Christ, ambassadors of Christ, the sons of God. If we go on their platforms, it is only so the word can go out to their subscribers. Once they disrespect you, you do not go back. Going back is like an abused child getting smacked around saying, May I have some more: they pat you on the head, good boy. Don’t bow to anybody, no Uncle Tom Negro, not Esau, not Moab. Bowing makes Christ look bad.

sense.text: “Now what time as Judas and Jonathan were in the land of Galaad, and Simon his brother in Galilee before Ptolemais, Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azarias, captains of the garrisons, heard of the valiant acts and warlike deeds which they had done. Wherefore they said, Let us also get us a name, and go fight against the heathen that are round about us.” These men wanted to make a name for themselves like Judas and his brethren.

They went toward Jamnia, Gorgias came out against them, Joseph and Azarias were put to flight, “and there were slain that day of the people of Israel about two thousand men. Thus was there a great overthrow among the children of Israel, because they were not obedient unto Judas and his brethren, but thought to do some valiant act.” The ones left in charge to watch over the people tried to be brave and make a name for themselves, and got people killed in the process: pretenders, not real leaders.

“Moreover these men came not of the seed of those, by whose hand deliverance was given unto Israel.” There is a certain seed the Lord raises up to bring forth deliverance to the people, and everybody is not that seed. Some are meant to watch the doors. There are many Israelites now who are Israel, but not the particular group the Lord is using to bring understanding to the people.

There is a special seed set up in each captivity: in Babylon’s time Daniel, Ezekiel, Jeremiah and Isaiah; in Persia Zerubbabel, Mordecai, Esther and Joshua; in Greece the Maccabees; in Christ’s time the disciples; and even now.
“Howbeit the man Judas and his brethren were greatly renowned in the sight of all Israel, and of all the heathen, wheresoever their name was heard of”: their names were known, even among the heathen.

“At that time certain priests, desirous to shew their valour, were slain in battle, for that they went out to fight unadvisedly.” You have to follow counsel and do as you are told, or you get yourself hurt. You are not cut out for that battle.

“Give not thine honour to another, nor the things that are profitable unto thee to a strange nation.” Our honour is our laws, our statutes, our commandments, the knowledge we have here: this truth.

The problem we always had in captivity and exile was sharing our knowledge with the nations, teaching them our laws while in exile, not ruling. We taught the Arabs the Bible, and they conquered us and established Islam. We taught the white man Judaism, and he conquered us and became a Jew. We taught the white man who came over here how to farm and survive the land, and he conquered us and called us illegal aliens.

Stop teaching the nations while we are in slavery; it is not their time. Now is our time to come together. When our king returns and puts us in authority and rulership, then we teach the nations.

“Now when word was brought unto Judas of Nicanor’s coming”, “they that were fearful, and distrusted the justice of God, fled, and conveyed themselves away.” Those who are fearful and run do not believe in God at all.

What is the justice of God? Recompensing vengeance to our enemies, taking us out of slavery, putting us in rulership and them in captivity. That is God’s justice. When you flee from that, you do not believe in God.

“For they, said he, trust in their weapons and boldness; but our confidence is in the Almighty who at a beck can cast down both them that come against us, and also all the world.” The nations trust in their weapons and boldness; our confidence is in the Almighty. If God wanted to, he could cast down the whole world for us.

Nicanor, “that took upon him to make good to the Romans their tribute by means of captives in Jerusalem, told abroad, that the Jews had God to fight for them, and therefore they could not be hurt, because they followed the laws that he gave them.” Our God fights for us when we follow his laws.

“Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is”: gathering together. That is why every opportunity we get, we come together, even on the heathen’s New Year, and open the schools.

“But exhorting one another”: these lessons and classes are to exhort you to see that these scriptures are real and this world is coming to an end. “And so much the more, as ye see the day approaching”: Christ is about to return. With all the war and the plagues and the things happening on the earth, gather together even more.

“Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.” To redeem the time is to understand the time we are living in, and the days we are living in are evil days.

That is why even in saying, let’s open the school tomorrow, we say if it is the Lord’s will. Anything can happen; some people leave the house and go back to the Lord. Train yourself always to say, Lord’s will, I’ll meet you there.
